s.faq.1: How does the phone agent get a number?
s.faq.2: After booking we set up a phone number (DE/AT/CH/TR/EU) via our telephony partner within 24 hours, or you forward your existing number when busy/out of hours. You set the greeting, voice and transfer number in the Studio.
s.faq.3: What happens if the agent doesn’t know something?
s.faq.4: It says so honestly, offers a call-back or transfer and hands over to your team. It never invents prices, deadlines or promises – that is firmly built into every role.
s.faq.5: Can an AI work for debt collection, a law firm or tax advisory?
s.faq.6: Yes, as an assistant: the agent takes in information, prepares, explains processes and creates drafts. Decisions, legal advice, tax advice and commitments stay with the professional – that is exactly how the roles are defined.
s.faq.7: Rent or buy – what’s the difference?
s.faq.8: Rent: a monthly fee, cancel monthly, fresh token allowance every month. Buy: pay once – setup, licence, a large starting credit (never expires) and 90 days of operation included. Then you choose: operation for €19, €29 or €39/month including tokens (depending on the agent’s tier) or your own Claude or DeepSeek key for a €9, €14 or €19/month platform fee – then you pay the AI directly to the provider.
s.faq.9: What does “your own AI key” mean?
s.faq.10: In the Studio under Connections you store your Claude or DeepSeek key (encrypted, only the last characters are shown). The agent then bills directly via your provider; ChatHelp deducts no tokens and charges only the small platform fee. If the key is invalid, you see it immediately in the Studio.
s.faq.12: The billing unit for all services. Guide values: a chat reply 6 tokens, a phone reply 8, a social post 5, a YouTube script 50. Tokens never expire and work for the Studio, widget, phone and API.
s.faq.13: How do I add the agent to my website?
s.faq.14: Activate the widget in the Studio and copy one line of code before the closing body tag of your page. Visitors chat with your agent, which only uses your knowledge base.
s.faq.15: How does the appointment agent book real appointments?
s.faq.16: In the Studio you enter services (duration, price), opening hours and slot interval. The agent only sees genuinely free times, books with a booking code, sends the confirmation with a calendar file and a reminder 24 hours before. Chat, phone, WhatsApp and your booking page write into the same calendar – double bookings are impossible.
s.faq.17: How does the ordering agent get onto my WhatsApp number?
s.faq.18: You connect your WhatsApp Business number via the Meta Cloud API. In the Studio you’ll find the webhook URL and verify token; setup takes about 15 minutes, and we can do it for you. After that every message goes to the agent, orders appear on the kitchen board, and drivers get the route via WhatsApp or SMS.
s.faq.19: Can the agent really dispatch taxis?
s.faq.20: Yes. Every ride lands on the dispatch live board with a ride code; the agent suggests the nearest free car or rank, and dispatch can reassign with one click. The driver gets the job in the driver app with navigation and taps “I’m here” – the customer receives an SMS with the car and plate. The agent quotes fares as estimates from your tariff; the meter is binding. The exception is fixed fares you store – to the airport, for example.
s.faq.21: How does the instant lead call-back work – is it allowed?
s.faq.22: When an enquiry comes in via a portal, your website form or email, the agent calls back within about 60 seconds – but only if the prospect has explicitly agreed to a call-back; the consent is documented. You set the calling window (e.g. Mon–Sat 8 a.m.–8 p.m.) and the maximum number of attempts. Every call is saved as a transcript, and the lead summary goes to you. Without consent the agent replies in writing instead of calling.
s.faq.23: How do I train my agent?
s.faq.24: In the Studio, without coding: import your website address, upload documents (PDF, Word, price lists), create FAQs with binding answers and set rules of conduct – tone, formal or informal, when a human takes over. You correct answers from real conversations right in the transcript; the correction applies from the next conversation. Before go-live a check runs with your test questions: you see a quality score and exactly which answers to refine.
s.faq.25: Does the phone agent sound like a human?
s.faq.26: It speaks with the latest generative speech synthesis – with breathing pauses, natural rhythm and short spoken sentences instead of read-out lists. You choose the language and voice (female or male). Asked whether it is human, it answers honestly – and still helps right away.

demo.marketing.title: Do the maths first, then advertise – campaigns that pay off.
demo.marketing.text: Example: Bohnenwerk coffee roastery, Cologne. Hanna runs the numbers on the Christmas campaign using real KPIs, splits the budget and evaluates the newsletter test – the figures come from the calculation tool, not from gut feeling. In live mode, you ask the questions.
demo.marketing.steps.0.1: Budget, margin, order value, conversion – from your knowledge base.
demo.marketing.steps.1.1: ROAS, cost per new customer, break-even and customer value – calculated exactly.
demo.marketing.steps.2.1: Budget per channel, Google and Meta ads, newsletters – ready to copy.
demo.marketing.steps.3.1: UTM links, A/B tests with significance, a report with next steps.
demo.marketing.script.0.2: Plan our Christmas campaign: €3,000 budget, goal: new coffee subscriptions.
demo.marketing.script.1.2: Here are the numbers: around 3,530 clicks and 85 new customers. The first order alone comes to about €1,230 in the red – but with the subscription, each customer is worth €167 in gross profit: LTV:CAC 4.7, payback in just over 5 months. It pays off if our ads focus on the subscription.
demo.marketing.script.2.2: Budget: €1,500 Meta, €900 Google Search, €400 retargeting, €200 testing. Plus three newsletters to 8,400 subscribers – the ads and emails are ready as drafts.
demo.marketing.script.3.2: Subject line test from the last newsletter: A 1,512 of 4,200 opened, B 1,638 of 4,200.
demo.marketing.script.4.2: B wins: 39% opens instead of 36%, so +8.3% – statistically significant (p = 0.005). We’ll use B’s style for all the Christmas emails.
demo.marketing.script.5.2: Campaign plan · 9 ads · 3 newsletters · UTM links ✓

demo.amazon.title: Margin, ads, stock – calculated with your real fees.
demo.amazon.text: Example: Bergwerk Outdoor, an Amazon brand from Cologne. Max runs the numbers on a price cut including the FBA fee, evaluates the PPC campaign and warns of a stock-out before Christmas – no review tricks. In live mode, you ask the questions.
demo.amazon.steps.0.1: Purchase cost, FBA fee, referral fee, storage, returns, advertising.
demo.amazon.steps.1.1: Exact per unit and per month – before every pricing decision.
demo.amazon.steps.2.1: ACoS, bids, negative keywords, title and search term check.
demo.amazon.steps.3.1: Days of cover, stock-out date, order quantity in cartons.
demo.amazon.script.0.2: Is the water bottle still worth it if I drop the price to €22.99?
demo.amazon.script.1.2: At €22.99 you keep €4.87 per unit after advertising – a 25.2% margin instead of 29.8%. The break-even ACoS drops from 31% to 27.7%. It only pays off if sales rise noticeably – otherwise you’re missing about €580 in profit a month.
demo.amazon.script.3.2: ACoS 30% – above your 25% target, but below break-even. Lower the bid from €0.62 to €0.52 and exclude “trinkflasche kinder” as a negative keyword.
demo.amazon.script.4.2: Stock: at 14 units a day, you’ll sell out on 6 December. Order 1,200 units now (30 cartons) and send 200 ahead by air freight.
demo.amazon.script.5.2: Price calculation · bid plan · order proposal ✓
